habitat: Marshes or damp vleis in otherwise dry thornveld and mixed bushveld, and rank vegetation bordering cultivations.
summary: A common resident. The breeding male is black, with a yellow-and-white shoulder, a pale grey bill that the description also calls blueish, and a broad tail that is often fanned. He twitters while displaying. The female and non-breeding male were not described. The Kemp paper name Whitewinged Widow and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Fan-tailed Widowbird has a red shoulder, retained all year, and a short tail. White-winged Widowbird has a yellow-and-white shoulder and a broad tail.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The female and non-breeding male were not described, which is why this needs review. The bill is pale grey on the identification line and blueish in the description. No flight photograph was found. A streaked Kruger frame was not used because that plumage was not described. Population figures and the Kemp name Whitewinged Widow were left unchanged.
